scenes.event: Elliott considers joining a late-night protest while his roommate Henry sleeps.
scenes.description: Elliott sits at his desk, staring at his laptop, surrounded by stacks of books and half-written essays. His roommate, Henry, lies on his bed, snoring softly. Outside, the distant sounds of a protest echo faintly through the window. Elliott wrestles with the choice between rest and civic duty.

characters.name: Elliott Walker
characters.description: A 22-year-old college student with a quiet intensity and a deep sense of responsibility. He is visibly tired but restless, his eyes reflecting a mix of exhaustion and determination.; Male / Student, 22 years old; Occupation: College student; Personality: Determined, Introspective, Idealistic, Resilient; Values: Social justice, Civic responsibility, Self-reflection; Interests: Political participation, Community activities, Personal growth; Experiences: Academic pressure, Political awakening, Late-night solitude, Friendship with Henry

characters.name: Henry Ramirez
characters.description: Elliott’s laid-back roommate, who prioritizes sleep and personal comfort; Male; Age: 20; Occupation: Undeclared college student; Personality: Lazy, indifferent, easygoing; Values: Comfort, routine, personal peace; Interests: Video games, streaming shows, sleeping; Experiences: Grew up in a stable suburban environment, has never attended a protest, often avoids stress-inducing situations.

actions.action: Looks out the window, listening to the protest.
actions.dialogue: Maybe I should go out there. I feel like I owe it to myself to be part of something bigger than my grades.

actions.action: Paces the room, trying to decide.
actions.dialogue: But if I don’t sleep, I won’t be able to do well on the presentation tomorrow. I’ve been so focused on my responsibilities, but what if I’m just avoiding something more important?

actions.action: Mumbles in his sleep, startling Elliott.
actions.dialogue: Eh? What? No, I’m not going out there again… too much yelling.
He’s right, it’s loud and tiring. But maybe that’s the point. Maybe I need to be there, to see it for myself.

actions.action: Packs a small bag with essentials and grabs a jacket.
actions.dialogue: I’ll go. Just for a while. I need to remember why I started caring in the first place.

scenes.plot: Elliott is torn between his academic responsibilities and his desire to participate in a late-night protest. After a moment of introspection and a brief interaction with his roommate, he decides to go out and engage in the event.
scenes.social_purpose: Elliott’s decision to join the protest highlights his values of civic responsibility and social justice, while also showcasing his personality traits of determination and idealism. The interaction with Henry adds a layer of contrast and prompts self-reflection.
